source.title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Lindelöf topological space in which every point is a Gδ-point. Must the cardinality of X be at most 2^ω?
accepted.context_brief: Cardinality of Lindelöf spaces with Gδ-points

evidence.quote:
Problem 1 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1969) . Suppose that X is a Lindel¨ of space such that every point of X is a G
δ-point. Then is it true that |X| ≤ 2ω?

A ”space” below is a Tychonoﬀ topological space. In particul ar, by a com-
pact space we mean a compact Hausdorﬀ space.

accepted.question_text: A space X is called weakly first-countable if for each x in X there is a decreasing sequence η_x = (V_n(x): n ∈ ω) with x ∈ V_n(x) such that a set U ⊆ X is open exactly when for every x ∈ U there exists n ∈ ω with V_n(x) ⊆ U. Does there exist, in ZFC, a weakly first-countable compact space X with cardinality strictly greater than 2^ω?
accepted.context_brief: Weakly first-countable compact spaces of large size

evidence.quote:
(wf c) A subset U of X is open if and only if for every x ∈ U there exists n ∈ ω
such that Vn(x) ⊂ U . In this case, we will say that the family {ηx : x ∈ X} is a weakly basic wf c-
structure on the space X. A space X is called weakly ﬁrst-countable if there exists
a weakly basic wf c-structure on X.

Problem 2 (Arhangel’skii, 1966) . Give an example in ZF C of a weakly ﬁrst-
countable compact space X such that |X| > 2
ω.

accepted.question_text: Using the same notion of weak first-countability given in the paper, does there exist, in ZFC, a compact space X that is weakly first-countable but not first-countable?
accepted.context_brief: Weakly first-countable but not first-countable compacta

evidence.quote:
A space X is called weakly ﬁrst-countable if there exists
a weakly basic wf c-structure on X.

Problem 3 (Arhangel’skii, < 1978). Give an example in ZF C of a weakly ﬁrst-
countable, but not ﬁrst-countable, compact space X.

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a weakly first-countable topological space and the Souslin number of X is countable. Must the cardinality of X be at most 2^ω?
accepted.context_brief: Weak first-countability with countable Souslin number

evidence.quote:
A space X is called weakly ﬁrst-countable if there exists
a weakly basic wf c-structure on X.

Problem 4 (Arhangel’skii, < 1980). Suppose that X is a weakly ﬁrst-countable space
such that the Souslin number of X is countable. Then is it true that |X| ≤ 2ω?

accepted.question_text: A space X is symmetrizable if its topology is generated by a symmetric d on X, meaning a non-negative real-valued function d with d(x,y)=0 exactly when x=y and d(x,y)=d(y,x), such that a subset A of X is closed exactly when d(x,A)>0 for every x in X\A. In every such symmetrizable space, must each point be a Gδ-point?

evidence.quote:
A symmetric on a set X is a non-negative
real-valued function d(, ) of two variables on X such that d(x, y) = 0 if and only if
x = y, and d(x, y) = d(y, x) for any x, y ∈ X. Suppose that X is a space and d is a
symmetric on X such that a subset A of X is closed in X if and only if d(x, A) > 0
for every x ∈ X \ A. Then we say that d generates the topology of the space X.
A space X is symmetrizable if the topology of X is generated by some symmetric
on X.
Problem 5 (< 1970). Is every point in a symmetrizable space a Gδ?

accepted.question_text: Must every pseudocompact symmetrizable space be first-countable?

evidence.quote:
A space X is symmetrizable if the topology of X is generated by some symmetric
on X.
Problem 6. Is every pseudocompact symmetrizable space ﬁrst-countabl e?

accepted.question_text: Must every pseudocompact symmetrizable space be a Moore space?
accepted.context_brief: Moore property for pseudocompact symmetrizable spaces

evidence.quote:
A pseudocompact symmetrizable ﬁrst-countable space needn ’t be metrizable
(this is witnessed by Mrowka’s space), but every such space i s a Moore space
(see [51]). Thus, the next question is a reformulation of Pro blem 6:
Problem 7. Is every pseudocompact symmetrizable space a Moore space?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a topological group that is countable, Fréchet-Urysohn, and non-metrizable?

evidence.quote:
Every ﬁrst-countable space X is Fr´ echet-Urysohn, that is, a point x ∈ X is in
the closure of a subset A of X only if some sequence in A converges to x.

Problem 8 (V. I. Malykhin, < 1980). Construct in ZF C a non-metrizable countable
Fr´ echet-Urysohn topological group.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a topological group that is extremally disconnected and non-discrete, where extremal disconnectedness means that the closure of every open subset is open?

evidence.quote: disconnected if the closure of every open subset of X is open.

Problem 9 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1967) . Construct in ZF C a non-discrete ex-
tremally disconnected topological group.

accepted.question_text: Let X be an arbitrary paracompact p-space, meaning a preimage of a metrizable space under a perfect mapping. Is the free topological group F(X) on X necessarily paracompact?

evidence.quote:
Problem 10 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1981) . Is the free topological group F (X) of an
arbitrary paracompact p-space X paracompact?

We remind that a paracompact p-space is a preimage of a metrizable space under a
perfect mapping [4].

accepted.question_text: Do there exist, in ZFC, countably compact topological groups G and H such that the product G × H is not countably compact?

evidence.quote:
Problem 11. Construct in ZF C countably compact topological groups G and H
such that their product G × H is not countably compact.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a countably compact topological group G whose square G × G fails to be countably compact?

evidence.quote:
Problem 12. Construct in ZF C a countably compact topological group G such that
its square G × G is not countably compact.

accepted.question_text: Must every infinite homogeneous compact space contain a non-trivial convergent sequence? Here a space X is homogeneous if for any x,y in X there exists a homeomorphism of X onto itself sending x to y.

evidence.quote:
a space X
is said to be homogeneous if for any x, y ∈ X there exists a homeomorphism h of
X onto itself such that h(x) = y.

Problem 13 (W. Rudin, 1956). Is it true that every inﬁnite homogeneous compact
space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary compact space Y, does there always exist a homogeneous compact space X and a continuous map from X onto Y?

evidence.quote:
Problem 14. Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact space Y as an image
of a homogeneous compact space X under a continuous mapping?

accepted.question_text: A compact space X is ω-monolithic if the closure of every countable subset of X is metrizable. Must every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space be first-countable?

evidence.quote:
A compact space X is
ω-monolithic if the closure of any countable subset of X is metrizable.

Problem 15 (Arhangel’skii, 1987) . Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact
space X ﬁrst-countable?

accepted.question_text: If X is a homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space, must the cardinality of X be at most 2^ω?

evidence.quote:
A compact space X is
ω-monolithic if the closure of any countable subset of X is metrizable.

Problem 16. Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space
X not greater than 2ω?

accepted.question_text: Must every nonempty monolithic compact space be first-countable at at least one point?

evidence.quote:
Problem 17. Is it true that every nonempty monolithic compact space is ﬁr st-
countable at some point?

More specifically, is dim preserved by t-equivalence at least within the class of separable metrizable spaces or within the class of compact spaces?

trace.notes: Resolved zbMATH record to the publisher article page and downloaded the article PDF; identified sections 2-7 as the open-problem regions containing Problems 1-20.
Extracted Problems 1-4 from sections on Lindelöf spaces and weakly first-countable spaces.
Extracted Problems 5-12 from the sections on symmetrizable spaces and topological groups.
Extracted Problems 13-20 from the sections on homogeneous compacta and t-equivalence.
Expanded compressed statements only with definitions and notation stated in the same paper, including weakly first-countable, symmetrizable, paracompact p-space, ω-monolithic, and t-equivalence.
No near-duplicate question statements were merged; the paper explicitly presents 20 distinct problem labels, though it notes that some are versions of the same question.

Accepted all 20 labeled problems because each had verbatim problem text in the PDF and any expanded context was recoverable from nearby source text; no item required unresolved cross-reference repair.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/selected-old-open-problems-in-general-topology.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
